title: Cylinder
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. Draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face. The first loop consists of four lines: draw a line from the origin to the point zero point zero five five one, zero; then from there to zero point zero five five one, zero point zero three three one; next to zero, zero point zero three three one; and finally back to the origin. The second loop also has four lines: start at the point zero point zero zero two two, zero point zero zero two two, and draw to zero point zero two six five, zero point zero zero two two; then to zero point zero two six five, zero point zero three zero nine; next to zero point zero zero two two, zero point zero three zero nine; and back to the starting point. The third loop is similarly composed of four lines: begin at zero point zero two eight seven, zero point zero zero two two, and draw to zero point zero five two nine, zero point zero zero two two; then to zero point zero five two nine, zero point zero three zero nine; next to zero point zero two eight seven, zero point zero three zero nine; and return to the starting point. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point zero five five one. Rotate the scaled sketch using the Euler angles negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and translate it using the translation vector zero, zero, and zero. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch zero point seven five units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body from this extrusion. The resulting shape is named the cylinder, which features a rectangular base with inner rectangles, a flat surface on the top and bottom, and dimensions of length zero point zero five five one four seven zero five eight eight two three five two nine four one, width zero point zero three three zero eight eight two three five two nine four one one seven six five, and height zero point seven five.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").workplane()

# Define the outer rectangle
sketch = sketch.moveTo(0.0, 0.0).lineTo(0.0551, 0.0).lineTo(0.0551, 0.0331).lineTo(0.0, 0.0331).close()

# Define the first inner rectangle
sketch = sketch.moveTo(0.0022, 0.0022).lineTo(0.0265, 0.0022).lineTo(0.0265, 0.0309).lineTo(0.0022, 0.0309).close()

# Define the second inner rectangle
sketch = sketch.moveTo(0.0287, 0.0022).lineTo(0.0529, 0.0022).lineTo(0.0529, 0.0309).lineTo(0.0287, 0.0309).close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will be the final model

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Overall dimensions
L = 0.7500   # length along X
W = 0.0551   # width along Y
H = 0.0331   # height along Z

# Wall thickness (derived so the two inner cells appear square)
t = 0.0111

# Outer rectangular bar
outer = cq.Workplane("XY").box(L, W, H, centered=(False, False, False))

# Two internal cell cavities (rectangular through-holes)
cell_w = (W - 3 * t) / 2.0    # width of each cell
cell_h = H - 2 * t            # height of each cell

hole1 = (cq.Workplane("YZ")
         .center(t + cell_w / 2.0, t + cell_h / 2.0)
         .rect(cell_w, cell_h)
         .extrude(L))

hole2 = (cq.Workplane("YZ")
         .center(2 * t + cell_w + cell_w / 2.0, t + cell_h / 2.0)
         .rect(cell_w, cell_h)
         .extrude(L))

# Cut the cavities to form the twin-cell hollow section
r = outer.cut(hole1).cut(hole2)
